correctness.rationale: For a nonzero shift row let r_x=|A∩(x+B)|. The sum of the r_x is 9, so prime Fourier uncertainty gives |supp V_g f|≥|A−B|(p+1)−9. Equality forces |A−B|=5 by Cauchy–Davenport; Vosper applies even at p=7 (5=p−2) and yields common-step progressions. For normalized supports with f(2)=g(2)=1, the central polynomial is z²+f(1)conj(g(1))z+f(0)conj(g(0)); the two adjacent roots are −f(0)conj(g(1))/f(1) and −f(1)conj(g(0))/conj(g(1)). The outer rows are nowhere zero. Exactly four cancellations means two distinct central roots and one root per adjacent row. The product of the two adjacent roots equals the central root product, and Vieta gives exactly the stated triples with nonzero denominators because p is odd. Conversely the formulas give precisely the four desired cancellations. The root-label fibers are closed in the equality locus by continuity of the corresponding Fourier evaluations, and hence open as their finite complements are closed. Each is homeomorphic to C× via f(1), proving the count of connected components, not merely path components.
residual_risks: The frozen threshold-based numerical check is not an independent exact proof; the verdict rests on the analytic reconstruction.
